proposal.title: Linquaqua: a passkey server library
proposal.summary: Linquaqua builds a passkey server library for developers of small web applications.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Small sites keep using passwords because passkey support is hard to add. Developers of small web applications depend on web authentication every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a passkey server library called Linquaqua. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Web authentication is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/linquaqua/linquaqua, which 39 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on web authentication for 5 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the Apache-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/linquaqua/linquaqua. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 7 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 97900.00 EUR for 65 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 500.00 EUR to 2450.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Small sites keep using passwords because passkey support is hard to add. Developers of small web applications depend on web authentication every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build a passkey server library called Linquaqua. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Web authentication is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We maintain http://forge.test/linquaqua/linquaqua, which 39 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on web authentication for 5 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the Apache-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/linquaqua/linquaqua. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 7 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 97900.00 EUR for 65 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 500.00 EUR to 2450.00 EUR.
